_comment: Nutrition per serving is computed at runtime from data/ingredients.json (see js/nutrition.js:calcRecipeNutrition). ingredients[].qty is in the unit defined for that ingredient (g/ml/pc).

recipes.name: Nasi Lemak (Lighter Version)
instructions: Rinse rice, cook with light coconut milk instead of full-cream for a lower-fat lemak flavour.
Pan-toast dried anchovies without oil until crisp; set aside.
Hard-boil or fry eggs with minimal oil.
Slice cucumber and plate alongside rice.
Top with sambal belacan, anchovies, peanuts and egg.
healthBenefits: Swapping full-cream coconut milk for light coconut milk cuts saturated fat while keeping the signature aroma.
Anchovies add calcium and omega-3s.

substitutions.note: Use brown rice for more fibre and a lower glycaemic load.

recipes.name: Hainanese Chicken Rice (Lean)
instructions: Poach chicken breast gently with ginger and garlic until just cooked (avoid overcooking to keep it moist without added fat).
Cook rice in a little of the poaching stock instead of oil-fried rice for fewer calories.
Slice chicken, serve over rice with cucumber and a low-sodium soy dip.
healthBenefits: Poaching instead of frying keeps this a lean, high-protein meal.
Low-sodium soy sauce reduces salt intake.

substitutions.note: Vegetarian swap: use firm tofu, poached the same way.

recipes.name: Curry Laksa (Reduced-Oil)
instructions: Fry laksa paste briefly in a non-stick pot with a splash of water instead of oil to cut fat.
Add light coconut milk and stock, simmer 10 minutes.
Add prawns and tofu, cook until prawns are pink.
Pour over blanched bee hoon, top with beansprouts and long beans.
healthBenefits: Light coconut milk keeps the creamy taste with roughly half the saturated fat.
Prawns and tofu provide lean protein.

substitutions.note: Use sliced chicken breast if shellfish allergy.

recipes.name: Mee Goreng Mamak (Veg-Boosted)
instructions: Stir-fry noodles in a hot wok with minimal oil (use a non-stick pan and a light spray).
Push noodles aside, scramble egg in the same pan.
Add tofu, cabbage, carrot and beansprouts; toss with low-sodium soy sauce.
Combine everything and serve hot.
healthBenefits: Extra cabbage and carrot roughly double the fibre and micronutrients versus a typical mamak portion.

recipes.name: Kolo Mee (Lean Style)
instructions: Blanch noodles and vegetables together, drain well.
Pan-fry lean minced beef with garlic until browned, no need for lard.
Toss noodles with a little soy sauce and top with the beef and vegetables.
healthBenefits: Skipping the traditional lard-rendered oil cuts a significant amount of saturated fat.

substitutions.note: Crumble and pan-fry tempeh for a vegetarian version.

recipes.name: Bee Hoon Soup with Chicken & Greens
instructions: Simmer chicken breast in water with ginger until cooked; shred.
Blanch bee hoon and kangkung in the same broth.
Combine in a bowl, season lightly with low-sodium soy sauce.
healthBenefits: A light, broth-based meal that's naturally lower in calories — good for a weight-loss day.

recipes.name: Wholemeal Chapati with Vegetable Curry
instructions: Knead wholemeal flour with water into a soft dough; rest 15 minutes and roll into thin chapatis.
Dry-cook chapatis on a hot flat pan (no oil needed).
Simmer chickpeas, carrot and eggplant with turmeric, garlic and light coconut milk until tender.
Serve curry with warm chapati.
healthBenefits: Wholemeal flour and chickpeas bring plenty of fibre and plant protein.

substitutions.note: Use roti canai dough occasionally as a treat — higher in fat.

recipes.name: Ikan Bakar (Grilled Spiced Fish)
instructions: Marinate fish with turmeric, garlic and ginger for 15 minutes.
Grill or air-fry (instead of deep-frying) until just cooked through.
Serve with a small side of sambal and brown rice.
healthBenefits: Grilling instead of deep-frying keeps this a lean, low-fat protein source ideal for muscle gain or fat loss.

recipes.name: Sayur Lodeh (Mixed Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Simmer vegetables and tofu in light coconut milk with turmeric until just tender.
Season lightly and serve with brown rice or on its own.
healthBenefits: High in fibre and low glycaemic impact — a good option for stable blood sugar.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Berries
instructions: Mix oats, milk and chia seeds in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with berries and a drizzle of honey before eating.
healthBenefits: Chia and oats provide soluble fibre that supports steady energy and satiety.

substitutions.note: Use yogurt instead of milk for a thicker, higher-protein version.

recipes.name: Greek Yogurt Protein Bowl
instructions: Slice banana over yogurt.
Sprinkle chia seeds and drizzle honey.
healthBenefits: High-protein, low-effort breakfast that supports muscle repair.

recipes.name: Vegetable Omelette
instructions: Whisk eggs, fold in finely chopped vegetables.
Cook in a lightly greased non-stick pan until set.
healthBenefits: High protein-to-calorie ratio; vegetables add fibre and vitamins.

recipes.name: Grilled Chicken Salad
instructions: Grill chicken breast seasoned simply with pepper and a little salt.
Toss chopped vegetables with olive oil.
Slice chicken over the salad.
healthBenefits: High-protein, high-fibre, calorie-controlled meal — great for a cutting phase.

substitutions.note: Grilled tempeh slices for a vegetarian version.

recipes.name: Quinoa & Tofu Buddha Bowl
instructions: Cook quinoa according to package directions.
Pan-sear tofu cubes until golden.
Steam broccoli and carrot.
Combine in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and soy sauce.
healthBenefits: Quinoa is a complete plant protein; combined with tofu this bowl covers all essential amino acids.

recipes.name: Teochew-Style Steamed Fish
instructions: Place fish on a plate with ginger, garlic and tomato.
Steam for 12–15 minutes until just cooked.
Finish with a splash of low-sodium soy sauce and steaming juices.
healthBenefits: Steaming keeps this virtually oil-free while preserving delicate fish protein and omega-3s.

recipes.name: Ulam-Style Herb Salad with Grilled Chicken
instructions: Grill chicken breast and slice.
Arrange raw ulam-style vegetables (cucumber, long beans, tomato).
Serve with a small portion of sambal belacan as dressing.
healthBenefits: A traditional low-calorie, high-fibre way of eating vegetables raw with minimal added fat.

recipes.name: Malaysian Fruit Bowl
instructions: Cube papaya and dragon fruit, slice banana, mix and chill.
healthBenefits: Papaya and dragon fruit are rich in vitamin C and fibre, and are naturally low glycaemic-load fruits.

recipes.name: Peanut Banana Protein Smoothie
instructions: Blend all ingredients until smooth.
healthBenefits: A calorie-dense, protein-rich snack useful for a muscle-gain phase.

recipes.name: Spiced Chickpea Snack
instructions: Toss chickpeas with turmeric and a little olive oil.
Roast or air-fry until lightly crisp.
healthBenefits: High fibre, plant-based protein snack that helps with satiety.

recipes.name: Tempeh & Vegetable Stir-Fry
instructions: Pan-fry tempeh cubes with garlic until golden.
Add broccoli and carrot, stir-fry until just tender.
Season with low-sodium soy sauce, serve over brown rice.
healthBenefits: Tempeh is fermented and rich in protein, fibre and probiotics.

recipes.name: Clear Vegetable & Chicken Soup
instructions: Simmer chicken thigh with ginger until tender, skim fat from the surface.
Add vegetables, cook until soft.
Season lightly and serve hot.
healthBenefits: A low-calorie, warming, high-volume meal that's satisfying without excess energy density.

recipes.name: Roti Canai with Egg (Occasional Treat)
instructions: Stretch and layer the dough, then pan-fry with a light amount of oil until flaky.
Crack egg onto the dough while cooking for roti telur.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed occasionally given the higher fat content — pair with a vegetable-based curry to balance the meal.

substitutions.note: Swap for wholemeal chapati as the everyday alternative.
